alate: Alate: the dorsum of the head deep yellowish brown, the dorsum of the thorax and abdomen brownish yellow and paler than the head, the venter of the abdomen yellow, the wings tinged with pale yellow. Compound eyes nearly round, ocelli elongate-round, the distance between the ocellus and the compound eye less than the width of the ocellus itself. Postclypeus extremely short, forming a transverse band, pale yellow and slightly raised, about one-quarter to one-third as long as wide; anteclypeus white and longer than the postclypeus; labrum pale yellow, rounded at the front. Antennae with 19–21 segments, mostly the third or fourth shorter. Head oval, widest behind the middle, narrower at both the anterior and posterior ends than at the middle; fontanelle aperture oval, narrow above and broad below, large and conspicuous, situated on a slightly projecting short tube at the front of the head and facing forwards. Mandibles sickle-shaped, their anterior part curved towards the midline, the base of the left mandible with a deep notch, in front of which are four small processes, successively smaller towards the front, the foremost behind the middle of the mandible, the rest of the mandibular surface smooth and toothless. Labrum nearly tongue-shaped, its front with an indistinct transparent point reaching half the length of the closed mandibles. Pronotum flat, narrower than the head, with a notch in the middle of both the anterior and posterior margins. Forewing scale larger than the hindwing scale, the wing membrane densely covered with fine short hairs; in the forewing the media arising independently at the humeral suture and closer to the cubitus than to the radial sector, the cubitus with 6–8 branches; in the hindwing the media arising from the base of the radial sector and, after arising, closer to the cubitus than to the radial sector, the cubitus with 7–8 branches.
biology: The colony is founded by a single reproductive pair and nests inside wood or tree trunks, where the nest temperature stays about 4 °C above ambient. In young colonies (up to 2.5 years) soldiers make up 10–15% of the population; the proportion falls with colony age, and mature colonies older than 8 years usually carry only 1–3%. Soldiers also grow larger: in a six-month-old nest the head width is under 0.99 mm, while in a 20-year-old laboratory colony it reaches 1.16–1.25 mm, an increase of more than a quarter. The first alates appear after about 8 years in the laboratory and 9–10 years in field burials, and a mature colony can produce more than 20,000 reproductives a year, with a total population of over 100,000 individuals. Swarming is concentrated in April–June, mostly between 18:20 and 22:00 at 21–30 °C. Foraging workers range up to 30 m from the nest, covering about 2,827 m². Three species of symbiotic protozoa are known from the gut, and three species of mites are common in nests, becoming numerous in weak colonies. The termite prefers sugar-rich material; sugarcane is among its favourite foods. The optimal temperature is 25–30 °C and activity is confined to 10–37 °C: all individuals die after 7 days at −3 °C, and 95% die within 2 days at 39–41 °C. Nest CO₂ is usually 0.5–6.5%, far above atmospheric levels.
distribution: In China distributed in the eastern part of the country, the northern limit roughly along and south of the line from Hefei, Chaoxian and Wuhu, Anhui, to Jianhu, Jiangsu, south of the Huai River at about 32–39° N; abroad recorded from Japan, the Philippines, the southern states of the United States, Hawaii and Africa.
soldier: Soldier: head and antennae pale yellow, mandibles blackish brown, abdomen milky white. The width of the head changes markedly with the age of the colony: in young colonies less than two and a half years old the head width is generally less than 0.99 mm, while after the colony matures the body gradually becomes larger, and in colonies that have developed for twenty years the head width may reach 1.16–1.25 mm, mature colonies being more than one-quarter broader than young ones; in addition, the pronotum and the number of antennal segments also increase with the development of the colony.
